prompt: Which parent categories earned a margin of at least 20 percent on their complete 2025 order lines? Use the sales table and keep the order lines with an order_date from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, both included, that have net_revenue_eur, units and unit_cost_eur all present. A line's margin is net_revenue_eur minus units times unit_cost_eur. Return two columns, in this order: parent_category and margin_pct, 100 times the sum of the line margins divided by the sum of net_revenue_eur, rounded to 1 decimal with ROUND(x, 1), so 15 percent is 15.0. Keep only the parent categories whose margin percentage, before rounding, is 20 or more. Return one row per parent_category. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, keep the complete 2025 lines, decide what one row stands for, write margin_pct, then write the group filter.
The 20 percent test is on a group total, so it belongs in HAVING, on the same percent scale as margin_pct and before rounding. "At least 20" includes 20 itself.
why_this_works: HAVING tests each category's total margin on the percent scale before rounding, and >= keeps a category that lands exactly on 20 percent.
